title: Calibration workflow rewrite and deterministic failover simulation for INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Rework the INT8 weight-only calibration pipeline to be deterministic, reduce noise in nightly regressions, and add a deterministic failover simulation harness that exercises GPTQ/AWQ profile transitions under traffic and kernel swap conditions. The goal is to reduce flaky regressions, improve signal-to-noise for golden-answer diffs, and provide a reproducible canary path for rollout automation.

Background: Current calibration and integration regressions suffer from non-deterministic seeds, large sample variance in prompt selection, and limited telemetry for cross-model drift. Multiple teams have observed spurious CI failures and difficulty reproducing canary regressions locally. We need a single, well-documented workflow that: 1) produces reproducible INT8 profiles for a given model+seed, 2) exercises production failover scenarios (kernel swap, profile fallback, model variant fallback), and 3) emits clear regression metrics that map to business SLOs (answer-delta rate, token-level KL, median latency delta).

Scope: Implement a calibration runner that: (a) accepts a deterministic seed and sample cohort spec (cohort sampling by intent/length/locale), (b) records a stable profile artifact with metadata (model hash, seed, hardware tag, compiler flags), (c) supports shadow-canary playback against live inference traces (sampled) and deterministic traffic replays, and (d) integrates into the nightly regression pipeline and the canary controller. Out of scope: full automation of rollback policies — this ticket provides the signal and playbooks; rollout automation will be follow-up work.

High-level approach:
- Build a standalone calibration CLI and library module that generates profile artifacts with an unambiguous metadata schema.
- Add a deterministic cohort selector that uses stratified sampling to reduce variance (length buckets, prompt category, language). Default cohort size: 10k prompts sampled with fixed seed.
- Produce golden seeds: store both unquantized (fp32) outputs and quantized (int8) outputs for the cohort; compute answer-delta metrics and stable fingerprints.
- Implement deterministic failover simulator: an orchestrator that replays traffic and injects failovers (e.g., kernel swap, profile mismatch, missing KV cache) with deterministic timing for reproducibility.
- Export telemetry: per-sample answer hash, token-level perplexity/KL approximations, generation latency, and a derived business metric "answer-delta-rate" with configurable threshold.

Trade-offs: Deterministic sampling and larger cohorts increase compute/time cost for nightly runs — mitigated by parallelization and by a low-cost small-cohort smoke run on every push. Storing FP32 golden outputs increases storage; we limit retention to golden seeds and compressed diffs for 90 days.

Acceptance Criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration runner produces an immutable profile artifact containing model hash, seed, cohort spec, hardware tag, and quantization hyperparams.
Nightly regression pipeline consumes the artifact and produces deterministic answer-delta metrics; rerunning with the same artifact and seed yields bit-stable metrics within documented epsilon.
Failover simulator can replay a saved trace and deterministically injects kernel swap and profile fallback events; test scenarios documented and runnable by SRE/Oncall.
Telemetry emitted to the console and observability backend: answer-delta-rate, token-KL-median, P95 latency delta, and percent of samples hitting quantization quality guardrails.
Runbook and playbook added to Confluence that describe how to interpret regressions and trigger manual rollback/canary pause.
Integration smoke test added to CI that runs a small 400-sample deterministic cohort on PRs changing quantization code paths.
Documentation and example usage of the CLI in the repo README and a reference GH PR linked in attachments.
Performance: nightly run time for full cohort completes within defined budget (<= 6 hours with parallel workers) and small-cohort smoke <= 20 minutes.
Security: artifacts are written with access-controls and keys consistent with Private deployment requirements (KMS tag present in metadata).
